Normalizes to -14 LUFS integrated. Great: Normalizes to -14 LUFS integrated. Great default target. Tracks mastered louder will be turned down; tracks mastered quieter will be turned up (risking limiting artifacts).
Normalizes to -14 LUFS (as of 2021). Tru: Normalizes to -14 LUFS (as of 2021). True peak limit of -1dBTP for stereo content. Content significantly louder than -14 LUFS will be turned down and may sound worse.
Normalizes to -14 LUFS (same as Spotify): Normalizes to -14 LUFS (same as Spotify). Also offers Ultra HD (24-bit/192kHz) which bypasses normalization. For standard streaming, aim for -14 LUFS.
Normalizes to -14 LUFS. Deezer uses the: Normalizes to -14 LUFS. Deezer uses the same loudness target as Spotify and YouTube. True peak at -1dBTP for safety.
SoundCloud does NOT normalize loudness. Master to -10 LUFS for competitive loudness. True peak limit of -1dBTP. 128kbps MP3 streaming reduces quality.
No loudness normalization. Fans can down: No loudness normalization. Fans can download original files (FLAC/WAV). Master to -12 LUFS for playback, but deliver unmastered high-res files for download.
CD (Red Book 16-bit PCM). Master between: CD (Red Book 16-bit PCM). Master between -8 to -12 LUFS with true peak at -0.3dBTP to avoid intersample peaks on consumer DACs.
Strict broadcast standard. EBU R128 (Eur: Strict broadcast standard. EBU R128 (Europe): -23 LUFS ±0.5 LU. ATSC A/85 (US): -24 LUFS. True peak ≤ -2dBTP. This is MUCH quieter than music. Required for TV/radio broadcast.
Podcasts need consistent loudness with l: Podcasts need consistent loudness with low dynamic range. -16 LUFS is the common target. True peak at -2dBTP for safety. Speech should sit at -16 LUFS with minimal variation (LRA 4-8).
No specific recommendation for this genr: No specific recommendation for this genre. Default to -14 LUFS (Spotify standard) as a safe starting point.
Foundation of the mix. Set kick first, t: Foundation of the mix. Set kick first, then build everything around it. Should be clearly audible but not overpowering.
Snare should cut through but sit slightl: Snare should cut through but sit slightly behind the kick. In rock/metal it may be closer to -8dB for punch.
Percussion adds texture and movement. Ke: Percussion adds texture and movement. Keep it low in the mix — barely noticeable when listening, but missed when removed.
Bass and kick should work together. If t: Bass and kick should work together. If they fight, you need sidechain compression. Bass should feel powerful without overwhelming the kick.
Lead vocals should sit ON TOP of the mix: Lead vocals should sit ON TOP of the mix, not buried in it. In pop, vocals are often the loudest element at -6dB. Use compression to maintain consistent level.
Backing vocals should support the lead,: Backing vocals should support the lead, not compete. Usually 6-8dB below lead vocals. Widen them with stereo delay/reverb for depth.
Guitars occupy the midrange — the busies: Guitars occupy the midrange — the busiest area of the mix. Use EQ to carve space. Acoustic guitars sit around -14dB, electric rhythm around -12dB.
Piano is wide-bandwidth and can easily c: Piano is wide-bandwidth and can easily clutter the mix. Use EQ to remove muddy lows and let other elements breathe. Pad/background keys at -18dB.
Strings add emotional depth but should s: Strings add emotional depth but should sit behind the main elements. They work best around -18dB to -14dB for pop, quieter for rock.
Synth leads should be prominent but not: Synth leads should be prominent but not overpowering. Bass synths sit closer to -12dB, lead synths around -10dB, pad synths at -16dB.
FX are accents — loud enough to be felt,: FX are accents — loud enough to be felt, quiet enough to not distract. Impacts may peak at -12dB, risers/sweeps at -20dB with automation.
Master bus should peak between -3dB and: Master bus should peak between -3dB and -1dB before mastering/limiting. True peak should never exceed 0dB. For streaming, aim for -14dB to -16dB integrated LUFS.
Adds spatial ambience by generating thou: Adds spatial ambience by generating thousands of decaying echoes. Essential for placing sounds in a virtual space — from tight rooms to massive cathedrals.
Repeats the input signal at a specified: Repeats the input signal at a specified time interval. Creates echo effects, rhythmic patterns, and spatial width when synced to tempo.
Mixes the signal with a modulated delaye: Mixes the signal with a modulated delayed copy (1-10ms). Creates a sweeping "jet-plane" effect through comb filtering.
Shifts the phase of the signal through a: Shifts the phase of the signal through all-pass filters, creating notch filters that sweep across the spectrum. Softer than flanging.
Modulates the AMPLITUDE (volume) of the: Modulates the AMPLITUDE (volume) of the signal at a rate controlled by an LFO. Creates rhythmic volume pulses.
Modulates the PITCH of the signal using: Modulates the PITCH of the signal using an LFO. Unlike chorus, no dry signal is mixed in — the pitch wavers continuously.
Adds harmonics by clipping or shaping th: Adds harmonics by clipping or shaping the waveform. Ranges from subtle warmth (tape saturation) to aggressive fuzz (hard clipping).
Reduces the dynamic range by attenuating: Reduces the dynamic range by attenuating signals above a threshold. Essential for controlling peaks and adding sustain.
Prevents the signal from exceeding a set: Prevents the signal from exceeding a set ceiling. The ultimate peak control — used on the master bus to prevent digital clipping.
Adjusts the balance between frequency co: Adjusts the balance between frequency components. The most fundamental mixing tool — cuts unwanted frequencies, boosts desirable ones.
Silences the signal when it falls below: Silences the signal when it falls below a threshold. Used to remove background noise, tighten drum tails, and create gated reverb effects.

30-50% for subtle movement, 50-70% for p: 30-50% for subtle movement, 50-70% for pronounced sweep
N/A (usually 100% wet — volume modulatio: N/A (usually 100% wet — volume modulation is the effect)

N/A (applied as an insert, not wet/dry m: N/A (applied as an insert, not wet/dry mix — use parallel compression instead)
N/A (brickwall limiter — always at 100%,: N/A (brickwall limiter — always at 100%, threshold controls the ceiling)
N/A (EQ is always applied to the full si: N/A (EQ is always applied to the full signal — boost/cut is the control)
N/A (gate is always 100% wet — threshold: N/A (gate is always 100% wet — threshold and range control the effect)
Matches Spotify's -14 LUFS target. TIDAL: Matches Spotify's -14 LUFS target. TIDAL Masters (MQA) may have different specs. HiFi tier plays original PCM (no normalization applied).
Film mixes are VERY quiet in LUFS becaus: Film mixes are VERY quiet in LUFS because they're played back in calibrated cinemas at high volume. -27 LUFS integrated is typical for theatrical mixes. Huge dynamic range (10-20 LU).
General mastering reference. -14 LUFS in: General mastering reference. -14 LUFS integrated with -1dBTP true peak is the "universal" target that works well across most platforms. Always leave headroom for the mastering engineer.
Hi-hats should be felt, not heard. If pe: Hi-hats should be felt, not heard. If people notice the hi-hat, it's probably too loud. Aim for -18dB to -20dB.
Claps sit between snare and hi-hat. They: Claps sit between snare and hi-hat. They add groove but shouldn't compete with the snare.
Toms should be slightly quieter than the: Toms should be slightly quieter than the snare. They're fills, not the main focus. Use automation if needed.
Copies the signal, modulates the copy's: Copies the signal, modulates the copy's pitch slightly, and mixes it back. Thickens sounds and creates lush, wide textures.
Uses \"Sound Check\" normalization to -1: Uses "Sound Check" normalization to -16 LUFS. More dynamic range than Spotify. Apple recommends -16 LUFS integrated with -1dBTP true peak. Dolby Atmos has separate requirements.

Pop music typically targets -14 to -12 L: Pop music typically targets -14 to -12 LUFS. Clean, consistent loudness with minimal dynamic range.
Rock benefits from punch. Master around: Rock benefits from punch. Master around -11 LUFS for impact while keeping some dynamics.
EDM/electronic is mastered loud. -10 LUF: EDM/electronic is mastered loud. -10 LUFS or even -8 LUFS for club/dance tracks.
Hip-hop/trap pushes loudness. -9 LUFS is: Hip-hop/trap pushes loudness. -9 LUFS is common, some go to -8 LUFS for competitive loudness.
Jazz preserves dynamics. -16 LUFS or qui: Jazz preserves dynamics. -16 LUFS or quieter allows natural dynamic expression.
Classical has wide dynamic range. -18 to: Classical has wide dynamic range. -18 to -24 LUFS is normal. Do NOT squash classical dynamics.
Metal is often heavily compressed and lo: Metal is often heavily compressed and loud. -9 LUFS is typical for modern metal productions.
R&B balances loudness with groove. -12 L: R&B balances loudness with groove. -12 LUFS is a good starting point.
Country music sits in the middle. -13 LU: Country music sits in the middle. -13 LUFS keeps things natural but present.
Latin music is energetic and loud. -11 L: Latin music is energetic and loud. -11 LUFS is a good target for competitive playback.
